title: Introduce per-tenant adaptive hedging and KV-sync backpressure for hosted inference
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers escalated production incidents where hosted inference requests experienced 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts during tenant bursts. Postmortem signals point to two compounding behaviors: (1) aggressive client-side retries and hedging causing a fanout amplification into the proxy and runtime, and (2) KV-cache sync churn between concurrent model replicas triggering transient cache misses and evictions that amplify per-request latency. This ticket proposes a coordinated mitigation: per-tenant adaptive hedging (dynamic hedging based on live latency percentiles and pool health) and a KV-sync backpressure mechanism that slows new inference fanout when replica cache warming is in progress.
scope: In-scope: implement adaptive hedging at the API gateway/proxy layer with tenant-scoped controls, build a lightweight KV-sync coordinator that exposes warming/rehydration state and backpressure signals to the request router, add telemetry for 95/99/99.9 latency with tenant tags, update SDK recommended retry/hedging defaults, and create a temporary emergency toggle for customer support. Out-of-scope: full redesign of KV cache algorithm, changes to model internals, Dedicated/Private on-prem installs beyond configuration knobs (we will provide guidance and patches after hosted rollout).
root_cause_analysis: 1) Retry amplification: customers with aggressive client-side retries + hedging (2 concurrent hedged requests by default) caused request multipliers during transient slowdowns.2) KV-cache desync: concurrent scaled replicas occasionally evicted identical prefixes during high churn; when a primary misses and followers are warming, requests hit slower paths leading to increased p50-p99 latencies.3) Connection exhaustion: proxy connection pool sizing per-tenant was not accounting for hedged fanout, leading to queueing and upstream 502/524 style failures. These combined to create retry storms and tenant-visible 5xx/timeouts during bursts.
proposal: 1) Adaptive hedging controller: implement logic at the router that measures per-tenant rolling latency percentiles and upstream error rates, and dynamically adjusts hedging and hedged concurrency. Default policy: disable hedging when p95 > configured threshold or when error rate > 2% for a tenant. Provide an override in tenant config and an emergency support toggle.2) KV-sync backpressure: introduce a simple coordination flag per model-replica-group that marks 'rehydrating' or 'warm'. Router will prefer replicas that report 'warm' and, when majority are rehydrating, will apply a mild head-of-line delay (e.g., 50-200ms jitter) and lower concurrency for that tenant until warm state clears.3) Connection/circuit controls: enforce per-tenant connection ceiling and per-route circuit breaker that trips early and returns graceful degrade responses with structured error payloads to advise clients to backoff.4) SDK guidance & telemetry: ship SDK patch to set conservative hedging defaults and update docs. Add new dashboards: tenant-latency-heatmap, kv-warm-state, hedging-adjustments timeline.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive hedging controller deployed behind feature flag and enabled for two pilot tenants
Observed reduction in hedged request multiplier by >=40% during tenant bursts in pilot tenants
KV-sync backpressure exposes 'warm' state and router respects it, with p99 latency improvement for warm-to-cold transitions by >=25%
Connection pool exhaustion events drop to baseline and 5xx spikes tied to tenant bursts reduce by >=60% in pilot window
Support emergency toggle can disable adaptive hedging immediately and is documented in runbook

Create dashboards and SLO alerts for tenant hedging metrics
Run closed pilot with 2-3 high-traffic tenants for 72 hours

notes: Trade-offs: adaptive hedging reduces amplification but adds routing complexity and small added latency when hedging is enabled. KV-sync backpressure is intentionally permissive (mild delays) to avoid adding long tail latency; may need tuning per model size. Long-term we should investigate KV-locality and stronger cache warming strategies but that is out-of-scope for this ticket.
estimated_risks: Edge cases where warm-state TTL mismatch could cause oscillation in router preference
Customer SDKs that re-enable aggressive hedging may negate router-level mitigations (need customer comms)
Risk of increased p50 due to mild head-of-line delays during warmup; must validate against p99 improvement target
